newsitem.title: UK: London freight - BFI dips on meagre fresh fixing.
newsitem.headline: London freight - BFI dips on meagre fresh fixing.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) dipped two points to 1,463 points, due to a scarcity of fresh fixtures reported, especially those on major grain routes.

Brokers said that the Biffex futures also fell for the same reason but that they were still looking for the market to bounce as soon as charterers start looking for tonnage to move the U.S. and Latin American grain crops around late March to April.
The only new grain fixing reported for a major route, was Tomen's booking for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain USGulf/Japan April at $25.50.
At the close the BIFFEX futures were 10 to 20 points easier. Most active March finished 18 points down at 1,535 after 22 lots traded. Total market volume was 44 lots.
On the timecharter sector, most new business focused on period charters, with Bestor 69,110 dwt taken by Interbulk delivery Japan April for around 12 months trading at $11,750 daily.
Other business saw GIC fix the Anangel Venture 69,406 dwt del Kobe, Japan March 4/10 for two to four months trading redel Singapore-Japan range at $12,000 daily.
In the mineral sector, Preag fixed 110,000 tonnes coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam and options April 1/15 at $6.85.
Ore business saw Farnet fix 160,000 tonnes Tubarao/Constanza March 15/20 at $7, while an undisclosed charterer fixed 120,000 tonnes from Goa to the same discharge port in Mar at $6.50.
Capers found mixed fortunes, with the Atlantic sector remaining weak for prompt shipments because of spare tonnage, while the Pacific region fared slightly better due to positional factors.
This situation was noted in Monday's Simpson, Spence and Young Atlantic Capesize Index, which rose 93 points to 4,037, and its Pacific Capesize Index which posted a gain of 64 points to 4,069.
